chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: Claude Hopkins band personnel: Howard Johnson, Shorty Horton, Walter Johnson
summary: He names saxophonists Howard Johnson and Benny Waters, trombonist Shorty Horton and drummer Walter Johnson, a gentleman, and notes Ovie Alston and Ed Hall had left.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Anybody that you remember particularly from the band? From the Claude Hopkins Band?

Claude Hopkins group? Yeah. Howard Johnson on the -- tenor piano, then, he was playing. Let's see, the banjo player, guitar player, who he had had -- been with him for years, hm, hm, hm, well let me move on. What the heck,
I know everybody that was in the band. Why can't I think of them? I cannot think.

Naturally Ovie Alston had gone, you know. He used to be there years ago, because he was the band. Bobby -- Bobby Johnson, Tenor saxophone player, yeah. I'll put it that way, and I'm trying to think who was playing the alto then, but Rudy -- we weren't together, but he had to have been in that band.
Tenor man, who used to be with Charlie --
(End of Tape Six.)
-- here we're talking about Johnny Haughton Horton, Shorty?
Yeah, Shorty Horton, uh-huh.
Shorty Horton is the trombonist.
Now was -- he was -- was he with Claude, or not?
Naw -- yes, he went with Claude. He was with Claude too.
Not when you were there.

I don't think so. I'm trying to -- I'm trying to -- I'm trying to remember. I want to be honest, because he and I worked with Fats, as I told you, and I'm telling you now, with Fats Waller, and he recorded 'In The Gloaming' with Fats on a big dance record, 12 inch thing, and 'Rump Steak Serenade,' you know, and what all, they was in the same session.
And he was a very good -- very fine trombonist, and a very fine (laughs) fellow. And we -- yes, we worked with Claude Hopkins.
You mentioned one of the saxophonists who was with Claude when you were with him was Benny Waters.
Benny Waters, yeah. Hmm, oh, Johnson.
Howard Johnson?
Howard Johnson.
One of the saxophonists. Who was the drummer? Do you remember?

Yes. Yes. Hm, hm, hm, by golly, oh, wait just a minute, who would have been playing drums then? Oh! Yeah, another Johnson, uh, uh, oh, he's working at a bank now. He's a bank messenger, guard, or something there. Walter Johnson.
Oh, Walter Johnson.
Walter Johnson, the most handsome -- (laughs) -- and what a nice man, what a nice drummer.
Had he been with Fletcher too?

Yes, Yes. He was with some of everybody, and they were proud to have him, proud to think about him, because every second that I've known him, every year that I've known him, I've never heard anybody say anything about Walter but a perfect gentleman, and I think it's kind of nice, you know?
